The '''eastern ruins''', commonly referred to simply as the '''ruins''' or sometimes the '''farm''', are the [[Update:Latest RuneScape News (8 May 2002)|remains of a village]] in the eastern [[Wilderness]]. They lie a [[single-way combat]] area in between level 26 to 29 Wilderness.

==Transportation==
Unlike many remains found within the Wilderness, these ruins cannot be reached by using [[Ancient Magicks]] [[teleportation]]. There are several transport options that place players near the ruins, however, listed here in order of least to greatest distance away:
* {{Plink|Games necklace}} — [[Corporeal Beast]], slightly south-east of the cave.
* {{Plink|Carrallanger Teleport}} — [[Graveyard of Shadows]], directly south of the ruins.
* {{Plink|Hunter cape}} — the hill just north of the ruins.
* {{plink|Canoe|pic=Paddle}} — the pond slightly north of the ruins.
* {{Plink|Ring of dueling}} — [[Ferox Enclave]], south of the ruins.
* {{Plink|Revenant cave teleport}} — [[Revenant Caves]], fairly north-west of the ruins.
* {{Plink|Burning amulet}} — the [[King Black Dragon Lair|King Black Dragon lair]], well north-west of the ruins.
The [[Wilderness Obelisk]] teleports to level 13, 19, and 35 Wilderness brings players a medium walk away.

==History==
The ruins' history is largely unknown. There are animal food troughs, crates, sacks, an ore, and a furnace, which all suggest that the area may have once served agricultural and industrial purposes. The lack of a teleport on the [[Ancient Magicks|Ancient spellbook]] indicates that they cannot be reliably traced back to the [[Zarosian Empire]].

=== Continuity ===
Despite the lack of in-game lore in ''Old School'' labeling the ruins as a farm, the animal pen indicates that it may well have been a farm at some point. However, the name of "farm" is purely a carry-over from ''RuneScape 3'', where the {{WP|Spirit of Summer}} quest takes place at a former farm. In the quest, it was not a village as stated by Jagex, but in fact a family farm from the late [[Fourth Age]] whose inhabitants were murdered by unknown assailants. Their souls were then fed on by the {{RSL|Spirit Beast}} before being eventually freed.

==Locations==
The main feature of the ruins is the [[Web Chasm|web chasm]] dungeon in the north-east corner. Inside is a [[singles-plus combat]] zone, where players can fight the spider boss [[Spindel]], a weaker version of [[Venenatis]]. There are also several buildings (or what's left of them) in the confines of the ruins.

The western building has a [[furnace]], which mysteriously still operates. Here players can smelt [[ore]]s, making it an option for those using the [[Hobgoblin Mine]] to the far north.

The central building also has a working sink which can be used to fill buckets with water, as well as two beds, indicating that the ruins are still used by some wanderers as cover.<gallery heights="200" mode="packed">
File:Ruins old building.png|A two-story building in the north of the ruins, possibly a former temple or church.
File:Abandoned farm pen.png|The long-abandoned animal pen, indicating livestock were kept here at one point.
File:Remains of an ancient beast.png|The remains of an ancient beast, possible predating the creation of the village due to their discoloration.
</gallery>

==Trivia==
[[File:Abandoned_farm_pen.png|thumb|width=400x400|The pen found in the eastern ruins.]]
[[File:Ruins old building.png|thumb|The building which uses the old wall textures and [[Pillar (Runic altar)|Runic altar pillars]].]]
* The ruins were a members-only area for over 2 months, until [[Update:Latest RuneScape News (8 May 2002)|8 May 2002]].
* A newspost calls this area the "overgrown village" shortly after its release, because the ruins were overrun with red vines in ''[[RuneScape Classic]]''. Other names from ''Classic'' are the "Grey Wolf Ruins," which was the name of the ruins on the map.
* The northernmost building has an inaccessible second floor, which is the only structure in the Wilderness that still uses the old wall textures from before the [[Update:Wilderness graphical update|2006 Wilderness graphical update]].
** This building is propped up by [[Pillar (Runic altar)|pillars]] which are the same as those found in [[runic altar]]s, and even include the examine "A part of an old temple."
*The furnace was originally on the eastern side of the ruins, although this was later changed.
